Donald Trump - who within mere months of his second term shoveled more than
_$[1 billion](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/3_h2uRk3bjI)_ of taxpayer money
into initiatives specifically designed to [inflate his personality
cult](https://zeteo.com/p/donald-trump-pyongyang) and make him feel better
about himself - lives in palpable fear of what several of his administration
officials are calling the possible coming flood of "de-Trumpification." The
"de-Trumpification" that keeps the U.S. president up at night isn't the kind
geared toward reversing the democratic backsliding that he and his Republican
Party have unleashed.

No, the "de-Trumpification" that the former reality-TV star is obsessed with
is the kind that would involve bulldozing his pet structural projects,
removing his likeness from money, and erasing the words "Donald J. Trump" from
some big, beautiful buildings once he's out of power, according to sources
close to the president.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Two Trump advisers and three U.S. government officials tell **Zeteo** that
Trump devotes an inordinate amount of his time not just to decorating, making
plays for his Washington, DC, arch and White House ballroom and other
expensive tributes to himself, and getting his face, name, and personal touch
plastered on as many buildings, pieces of currency, and monuments as he can
possibly get away with; the American ruler also spends what one administration
official describes as "a ton" of time worrying about - and using considerable
government resources to preempt - future efforts by Democrats to tear down his
presidential legacy of architecture and idolatry.
